ledger.note: 1702: Portugal's Timor colony begins at Lifau. Infobox 'Establishment: 1702'; a governor 'was sent to Lifau, which became the capital of all Portuguese dependencies in the Lesser Sunda Islands'. The first Europeans arrived in 1515 and Dominican friars founded Lifau in 1556. The page names no extent; Timor and the Flores cluster are the researcher's reading.
1769: the capital moves from Lifau to Dili (infobox 'Lifau (1702-69)'; 'Dili (1769-1942; 1945-75)').

ledger.note: 1769: Ambeno leaves the Portuguese area. The page says only that the capital moved from Lifau (in Oecusse) to Dili; the 1859 treaty page speaks of the Netherlands 'ceding' Ambeno to Portugal. Which year Ambeno was lost, and to whom, is not on either page; the Dutch company is the researcher's guess for the claimant. region.text: Larantuka, Sikka and Paga on Flores, Wouré on Adonara, Pamung Kaju on Solor

ledger.note: 20 April 1859: Portugal gives up the Flores cluster. The Treaty of Lisbon: Portugal ceded 'Larantuka, Sikka, and Paga on Flores; Wouré on Adonara; and Pamung Kaju on Solor' to the Netherlands (ratified 18 August 1860); the Dutch cancelled a 1851 debt of 80,000 florins and paid 120,000 florins more.

ledger.note: 20 April 1859: Portugal receives Maubara and Ambeno. 'The kingdoms of Maubara and Ambeno on Timor' passed from the Netherlands to Portugal, which also got Dutch renunciation of 'any claim to the island of Atauro'; the treaty 'establishes the boundaries between Portuguese and Dutch territories on the island of Timor' and 'defines the limits of Oecusse'. The page does not mention Citrana.

certainty.note: The page gives no extent; Portuguese authority outside the coast and the capital was thin, and the 'dependencies' were kingdoms (liurai) under Topasses and Dominicans.

The treaty of 20 April 1859 'establishes the boundaries' on Timor, the 1904 treaty exchanged enclaves and 'The definitive border was established by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 1914 and ratified in 1916'.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch. A colony Cliopatria draws inside its Portuguese Colonies row (1640-1910: East Timor 52 of 54 cells, Ambeno and Liquica included, plus two Flores cells) and Estado Novo row (1926-1975); this dossier keeps those cells but dates the colony from the page's 1702 and explains the 1859 changes. Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the page gives no extent before 1859: the 1702 shape is the final country plus the Flores cluster read from the 1859 treaty page; (2) the 1769 loss of Ambeno is a bridge (confidence 1): the treaty page says the Netherlands 'ceded' Ambeno and Maubara in 1859, the Timor page says only that the capital moved; if the sa-06 review of Portuguese Colonies keeps Ambeno Portuguese throughout, drop that event and the 1769 keyframe's exclusion; (3) Citrana, Jaco, the 1893 convention and the Oecusse exchange are not on the pages (the Lisbon page speaks of Ambeno, not Citrana); (4) the end: Portugal never formally ceded the territory; the dossier ends on Fretilin's declaration (28 November 1975), as the east-timor dossier begins; (5) Noimuti's coordinates and Maucatar's district are the researcher's; (6) Atauro was Portuguese territory before 1859 (the Dutch relinquished a claim in the treaty); it sits in Dili district and is covered by the country shape; (7) Lifau's coordinates are approximate; (8) no rulers strip: the page does not list the governors. Gazetteer: Larantuka, Solor, Adonara, Sikka, Paga, Maubara, Maucatar, Noimuti, Lifau and Atauro are not in the gazetteer; discs and districts stand in. The Estado Novo dossier (eu-21) should drop East Timor from its 1926-1975 shapes or keep it as a vassal tint of this colony.
